# 0x209 — `engine_gear`

DLC 6 · 100 Hz · status: **confirmed**

Engine speed, gear position, riding mode and traction-control level in one frame.

## Layout

Bytes are numbered from 0. Multi-byte values are big-endian unless a row says otherwise. Bit 7 is the most significant bit of a byte.

| Byte | Content |
|---|---|
| B0 | `engine_rpm` |
| B1 | `engine_rpm` |
| B2 | `b2_unknown` |
| B3 | `gear_actual`, `tcs_level`, `start_flag` |
| B4 | `gear_requested`, `b4_bit3_unknown`, `ride_mode` |
| B5 | `shift_window_bits` |

## Signals

| Signal | Where | Type | Value | Unit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine_rpm` | B0:B1 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.390625 | rpm | confirmed (high) |
| `b2_unknown` | B2 | uint8 | raw |  | unknown |

### `engine_rpm`

Engine speed, raw × 25/64.

**Confirmed by:** OBD-II PID 0x0C on the same bus; the exhaust-note frequency on the camera sound track.

**How we know:** Compared with OBD-II PID 0x0C polled on the same bus: median difference +0.1 % over 96 pairs in three sessions, steady pairs within 0.3 %.

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 7330.5 rpm

### `b2_unknown`

Changes with road speed (correlation 0.99 with rear wheel speed over one ride). Not decoded.

### `gear_actual`

Gear reported by the gearbox sensor. Never reads 7. With the engine stopped it reads 0 whatever gear is engaged, so use `gear_requested` for a display.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | neutral |
| 1 | 1st |
| 2 | 2nd |
| 3 | 3rd |
| 4 | 4th |
| 5 | 5th |
| 6 | 6th |

**Confirmed by:** Published gearbox ratios, through engine speed divided by wheel speed.

**How we know:** rpm divided by rear wheel speed gives one constant per gear (about 105.8, 80.1, 66.7, 56.8, 49.0, 42.7), the same within 0.2 on five rides. Relative to 3rd gear that is 1.588, 1.203, 1, 0.853, 0.735, 0.640; the gearbox ratios Yamaha publishes (2.571, 1.947, 1.619, 1.381, 1.190, 1.037) give 1.588, 1.203, 1, 0.853, 0.735, 0.641.

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 3 gear

### `tcs_level`

Traction-control level in effect: a copy of 0x226 `tcs_level` (B0 bits 3..2), not of the mode the dash shows (0x226 `tcs_mode`). In the TCS 1 and TCS 2 modes the two are equal. In M (manual) this field carries the TCS level the rider set inside M, while the dash shows "M". Value 0 is probably TCS OFF, which this bike offers, but that is not confirmed: it appeared on one ride only, and nobody noted TCS OFF being selected on it. No capture has a deliberate switch to OFF yet.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | probably TCS OFF (not confirmed) |
| 1 | TCS level 1 |
| 2 | TCS level 2 |
| 3 | TCS level 3 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers, through 0x226; the rider's own Manual setting.

**How we know:** Equal to 0x226 B0 bits 3..2 in 796 198 of 796 307 paired frames over five recordings of one day; the rest are the first frames after power-on and a one-frame lag at a change. Equal to 0x226 B3 in only 792 600 of them: every mismatch is M with the manual TCS level at 2, and when the rider raised it to 3 inside M, this field went 2 -> 3 within 10 ms of 0x226 B0. Earlier rides agreed with 0x226 B3 in more than 420 000 frames because the rider's M setup then had TCS 3. 13 rider-made changes across levels 1, 2 and M on earlier rides.

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 3

### `start_flag`

Set while the engine is cranking: in 13 of 13 engine starts it comes on with the first cranking frame and clears 0.7-0.9 s later when the engine idles; the same at nine more starts on a later ride (0.7-1.0 s). It is also set for about 0.1 s just before every key-off, but not when the engine stops with the ignition left on. On some rides it is set for long stretches with the ignition on and the engine off, so the exact meaning is open. It is not a shift flag: clear at all 535 gear changes checked.

### `gear_requested`

Gear position as the shift mechanism sees it. Reads 7 for a moment during gear changes between 2nd and 6th while moving; changes between 1st and 2nd go straight from one number to the other. Keeps showing the engaged gear with the engine stopped, which is what the dash shows. Mask with 0x07: bit 3 of the byte is a separate flag.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | neutral |
| 1 | 1st |
| 2 | 2nd |
| 3 | 3rd |
| 4 | 4th |
| 5 | 5th |
| 6 | 6th |
| 7 | between gears |

**Confirmed by:** Gear changes on rides; the dash gear indicator with the engine stopped.

**How we know:** One 43-minute ride: 74 episodes of 7, one per gear change above 2nd, symmetric up and down. The same pattern on a second ride at full rate.

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 3 gear

### `b4_bit3_unknown`

Set for about half a second at every bus wake-up, and for the whole time `tcs_level` reads 0 on the one ride where that happened.

### `ride_mode`

Selected riding mode. The same two bits appear in 0x215 B7 and 0x226 B0.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | D-MODE 1 |
| 1 | D-MODE 2 |
| 2 | D-MODE 3 |
| 3 | D-MODE 4 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers.

**How we know:** The rider stepped through the four modes with the dash in the frame in two parked sessions; the field followed every step. The three copies agree on every ride.

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 0

### `shift_window_bits`

B5 takes the values 0x00, 0x04 and 0x08. 0x08 goes with an open throttle and 0x04 with a closed throttle and the clutch engaged, but 0x08 never occurs in 6th gear and 0x04 never occurs in 1st. That fits "upshift possible" (bit 3) and "downshift possible" (bit 2), the two quickshifter windows, better than a plain drive/overrun state. A later full-rate ride agrees: 0x04 never in 1st (0 of 81 037 frames above 1500 rpm), 0x08 in 1st to 5th (6th was not used). Quickshifts show in this byte: on 57 of 57 upshifts with the throttle open it goes 0x08 -> 0x00 for about 300 ms, starting about 50 ms before the gear changes, while the throttle valve stays open and the engine speed dips (ignition cut); on 76 downshifts 0x04 -> 0x00 for about 230 ms, with the throttle valve blipped open while the grip stays closed in 83 % of them. The rider's quickshifter on/off settings are separate bits (0x226 `qs_up_enabled`, `qs_down_enabled`); they were switched only with the engine off, so they do not test this byte yet.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | neither |
| 1 | bit 2 only |
| 2 | bit 3 only |

**Example:** `0x209  49 4E 07 66 03 08` → 2

> In the first ~0.55 s after the bus wakes, B4 reads 0x48/0x49 and then 0x08/0x09 before settling. Ignore the frame until then.
